cards.explanation: The answer is Philippi, friends. The text calls it a Roman colony and the leading city of that district of Macedonia (Acts 16:12). Paul and his team stay there several days. Big city, and a lot happens in it.

The answer is False, friends. The text says they sat down and spoke to the women who had gathered there (Acts 16:13). It was a riverside meeting outside the city gate, at a place of prayer. And a woman in that very group is about to matter a lot.

The answer is the Lord, friends. The text says, “The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.” (Acts 16:14) Paul does the speaking, but the opening is the Lord's doing. Lydia, the dealer in purple cloth, listens and responds.

The answer is False, friends. Lydia urges them, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” The writer adds, “And she persuaded us.” (Acts 16:15) The team ends up at her house, and the story comes back to it at the very end. Her door stays open.

The answer is that they serve the Most High God, friends. She shouts, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!” (Acts 16:17) She follows Paul and the team while she says it. The text only tells us what she shouts, so I'll leave it there.

The answer is Jesus Christ, friends. Paul says, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” (Acts 16:18) He doesn't command it in his own name. He goes straight to the name of Jesus Christ.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “And the spirit left her at that very moment.” (Acts 16:18) No waiting around and no second try. Paul gives the command in the name of Jesus Christ, and it happens right then.

The answer is that they drag them before the authorities, friends. The owners “…seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.” (Acts 16:19) Silas is Paul's traveling partner, and he gets dragged along too. They did this when they saw their hope of making money was gone.

The answer is throwing the city into turmoil, friends. The owners say, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil” (Acts 16:20). Then they add a charge about customs unlawful for Romans (Acts 16:21). Notice what charge they lead with.

The answer is that he fastens their feet in stocks in the inner cell, friends. The jailer “…placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.” (Acts 16:24) He got the order to guard them securely, and that's how he carries it out. It's a hard moment for Paul and Silas, so let's just say it plainly.

The answer is praying and singing hymns to God, friends. “About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God…” (Acts 16:25) Silas is Paul's traveling partner. The two of them are in the inner cell with their feet in the stocks after a beating (Acts 16:23-24). That's not what I would be doing at midnight.
The answer is True, friends. The text says, “…the other prisoners were listening to them.” (Acts 16:25) Paul and Silas weren't singing to nobody. Even in that prison, somebody was paying attention.

The answer is False, friends. “At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.” (Acts 16:26) It's everyone's chains, not just Paul's and Silas's. The earthquake shook the foundations of the prison, and the doors flew open too.

The answer is “We are all here,” friends. Paul calls out, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!” (Acts 16:28) The jailer had presumed the prisoners had escaped (Acts 16:27). This is a heavy moment, and I think Paul's words come right when they're needed.

The answer is “What must I do to be saved,” friends. The jailer asks, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?” (Acts 16:30) He asks it after he rushes in and falls trembling before Paul and Silas. Not a small question, and it gets a direct answer.

The answer is believe, friends. Paul and Silas reply, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.” (Acts 16:31) It's a short answer to a big question. And the household is included in it.

The answer is False, friends. “At that hour of the night…” the jailer takes them and washes their wounds, and “…without delay, he and all his household were baptized.” (Acts 16:33) No waiting at all. The whole household is included.

The answer is that they have come to believe in God, friends. The text says, “…he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.” (Acts 16:34) The jailer brought Paul and Silas into his home. He set a meal before them. I think that's a happy house.

The answer is citizens, friends. Paul says they were beaten publicly without a trial and thrown into prison, “…even though we are Roman citizens.” (Acts 16:37) That fact is what alarms the magistrates (Acts 16:38). One word, big change in the room.

The answer is that the magistrates should come themselves and escort them out, friends. Paul says, “Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!” (Acts 16:37) He won't accept being sent off secretly. And the magistrates do come themselves (Acts 16:39).

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them.” (Acts 16:40) Lydia's door was open to them before the trouble and after it. Then they left the city.
